transcript.content: Hello. I am Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hi Dr. Smith. What brings me in... I guess it's that I feel like I'm always moving from one thing to the next, you know? Like I just can't idle. It's funny, my wife says I'm like that old lawnmower we used to have, the one that wouldn't shut off unless you pulled the spark plug wire. We had this huge yard back in Ohio, took me three hours to mow it every Saturday. Anyway, the new work setup has made it a lot harder to hide that I can't sit still. They put us all in these open-plan pods now, which is just ridiculous if you ask me. The lighting in there gives me a headache too, it's that weird blue fluorescent kind. But yeah, the constant moving around is why I'm here.
Looking back at your life, have you always felt this way, even when you were a child?

Oh, yeah, definitely. I mean, looking back, this was around long before the new job setup. Even in grade school, my teachers were always writing on my report cards that I was bright but careless, you know? They said I talked out of turn and always had to be reminded to stay with my work. It's funny thinking about grade school, I went to this little brick schoolhouse, Lincoln Elementary. They tore it down a few years ago to build a strip mall. Such a shame, really. I remember Mrs. Gable, my third-grade teacher, she had this massive collection of porcelain frogs on her desk. Hundreds of them. I knocked one over once when I was supposed to be in my seat... broke its little leg off. I tried to glue it back on with that white paste we used to use, but it never looked right again. But anyway, yeah, I've always been like this.
Beyond the constant need to move, do you often find that you have trouble focusing on tasks or that you frequently make careless mistakes?

Yeah, the careless mistakes... that happens a lot, actually. Like at work, I do customer service, right? And I’ll think I’ve completely finished a customer ticket, everything's good to go. But then later I’ll notice I typed the wrong account number, or I just totally skipped one of the required boxes. Or I'll miss one little instruction that makes the whole thing come back to me. 

Speaking of things coming back, the new software system they gave us is just a nightmare for that. They rolled it out right around Halloween. I remember because my neighbor had this giant inflatable spider on his roof, and the wind kept blowing its legs over onto my side of the property line and into my gutters. I had to get the ladder out twice to push it away, and my gutters really needed cleaning anyway... they get completely choked up with oak leaves this time of year. We have this massive oak tree in the front yard, probably a hundred years old. Drops leaves from October straight through Thanksgiving. But anyway, yeah, the new software has all these tiny little fields on the screen, so it's really easy for me to miss one little box, and then the ticket just bounces right back to my queue.
In your daily life as an adult, do you frequently find yourself acting impulsively, such as blurting out answers, interrupting others, or having difficulty waiting your turn?

Yeah, I guess... I mean, I really don't mean to be rude about it, but at work, if I hear my coworkers trying to work through a customer problem, I’ll just jump right in with an answer before they’ve even finished explaining it. Or before anyone even asked me for help, honestly. It just sort of comes out. 

Speaking of my coworkers, the guy in the pod next to me, Gary, he just got this new car. It's one of those electric ones, completely silent. I almost walked right into it in the parking lot on Tuesday. Scared the living daylights out of me. I don't trust a car you can't hear running. My first car was a '78 Chevy Nova, and believe me, you could hear that thing coming from three blocks away. Needed a new muffler every other year, it felt like. I used to take it down to this guy Sal on 4th Street, he had a shop behind the old diner. Best mechanic I ever knew, though his waiting room always smelled like burnt coffee. 

But anyway, what were we... oh, right, interrupting. Yeah, I definitely do that a lot with the other reps.
When you are working on those customer tickets, do you find that you have a hard time staying focused on the task until it is completed, or is it mostly just the careless mistakes that happen?

Well, it's not just the mistakes, honestly. Staying focused is... it's a real struggle. Especially when things drag on. Like, if they pull us into one of those longer coaching meetings, or if I have to read through a new procedure manual. I'll start off okay, but after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes are just moving across the page, or I'm looking right at the supervisor, but I haven't taken in a single word they said for the last five minutes. 

Those coaching meetings, they always hold them in Conference Room B. I don't know who designed that room, but the fluorescent lights in there have this awful hum. It's like a low-grade buzzing right in your ear. It reminds me of the refrigerator in my first apartment. That thing used to vibrate so loud it would rattle the ice cube trays. I lived above a bakery back then, right on Main Street. The smell of fresh bread at 4:00 AM was incredible, but the baker, Tony, he'd play opera music while he worked. Full blast. Just Pavarotti echoing up through the floorboards while my fridge buzzed along with it. Tony made these amazing cannolis, though. Real ricotta, none of that cheap filler. 

But yeah, when I'm reading those procedures or in those meetings, my attention just drifts off completely, and I have to go back and re-read the same paragraph three times just to figure out what I'm supposed to be doing.

Beyond the restlessness you mentioned, do you find that you frequently have an internal sense of being 'driven by a motor' or an inability to stay still even when you are trying to relax, such as while watching a movie or sitting at home?

Yeah, it's exactly like that. Even when I'm supposed to be relaxing, you know? Like, if it's a quiet night and I'm trying to read at home, or if my wife and I are sitting down to watch a movie... I just can't last very long before I'm shifting around on the couch, or I start commenting on the movie, or I just have to get up and grab a glass of water or something. 

My wife, she loves those long historical dramas. We tried watching that one about the royal family last weekend. She gets so into the costumes and all the little details. Speaking of costumes, my grandson was a pirate for Halloween this year. He had this little plastic sword that lit up, and he kept swinging it at the dog. The dog's a golden retriever mix, absolute sweetheart, but he kept trying to eat the sword. We got him from a rescue down in the next county over. The lady who ran the rescue, she had this huge property with horses, too. I always thought it would be nice to have horses, but the feed bills must be astronomical. Plus, you need a good fence. I spent three weekends last summer just repairing the chain link in my backyard because the neighbor's kid backed his dirt bike into it. 

But anyway, yeah... sitting through a movie is tough. I just feel like I need to be doing something, even when I'm supposed to be taking it easy.

Looking back at the past six months, would you say that you experience more difficulty with inattention, more difficulty with hyperactivity and impulsivity, or do you feel that both are equally problematic for you?

Gosh, looking back... I really couldn't tell you if one is worse than the other, to be honest. Six months... let's see, six months ago was right around the time my brother-in-law, Dave, came to visit. He stayed with us for two weeks and parked his RV right in our driveway. It's a beautiful rig, one of those big ones with the slide-outs. But the thing was so huge it completely blocked my wife's flower beds, and she was just furious. 

She spends hours out there with her hydrangeas. You know, you have to get the soil acidity just right or they change color on you. I think you need to mix in coffee grounds if you want the blue ones? Or maybe that makes them pink. I can never remember. We used to drink a lot of coffee, but I started trying to cut back, so now I drink this herbal tea stuff my wife buys. Tastes like hot lawn clippings, if I'm being perfectly honest. I don't know how people drink it every morning. The box says it has chamomile and lemongrass, but it mostly just smells like the back of a lawnmower. 

But anyway... what were you asking? Oh, right, if the focus or the fidgeting is worse. Yeah, I really couldn't say. They both just sort of happen, so I've never really kept track of which one is a bigger problem.
